patterns_data.top_pattern: OH LTSS Dual Eligible SNF spend jumped on both volume and rate
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Medicaid LTSS Dual Eligible / SNF - FREE STANDING
patterns_data.pattern_details: Ohio free-standing SNF spend for LTSS Dual Eligible members rose sharply across both authorization statuses. Most of the increase came from non-PA claims, but the PA-required slice also showed more admissions and higher paid per admit. This is a combined utilization and reimbursement issue in one facility type, not just a broad Medicaid trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A concentrated $50M-plus SNF increase creates a large, actionable lever for UM, pricing, and network teams.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint OH SNF review for LTSS Dual Eligible members covering admission growth, level-of-care decisions, and free-standing SNF reimbursement terms.
evidence_summary: OH LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNF spend increased by +$50.3M across PA-required and non-PA claims.
The non-PA slice drove +$40.1M with 5,772 more admissions and about +$6,949 paid per admit.
The PA-required slice added +$10.2M with 977 more admissions and about +$10,462 paid per admit.

patterns_data.top_pattern: OH TANF Standard SNF growth is blurred by a large Not Mapped bucket
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Medicaid TANF Standard / SNF - FREE STANDING and Not Mapped
patterns_data.pattern_details: Ohio TANF Standard costs rose through two different mechanisms: a large SNF volume increase in non-PA claims and a separate authorized bucket recorded as Not Mapped with very high paid per admit. Because a material share of the increase sits in an unmapped facility category, facility classification needs to be corrected before broad site-of-care or pricing action. After validation, the remaining SNF growth should be managed through admission and level-of-care controls.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the Not Mapped bucket is misclassified, the plan could misread where TANF Standard spend is actually occurring and act on the wrong setting.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Correct the OH facility mapping for the authorized TANF Standard spend, then run a targeted SNF admission and reimbursement review on the validated population.
patterns_data.validation_reason: A +$10.1M authorized increase is sitting in a Not Mapped facility category, so site-of-care interpretation is not reliable until mapping is fixed.
evidence_summary: OH TANF Standard spend increased by +$19.1M across SNF and Not Mapped facility classifications.
The Not Mapped authorized bucket added +$10.1M with 408 more admissions and about +$21.6K paid per admit.
The non-PA free-standing SNF bucket added +$9.1M with 1,314 more admissions while paid per admit was nearly flat.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorization-code shifts are creating false cost signals in CA, IN, and TN
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Medicaid authorization coding across hospital claims
key_driver_codes: Other Kidney and Urinary Tract Diagnoses with CC
Cirrhosis and Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Several states show material movement in authorization-code assignment rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement story. California, Indiana, and Tennessee each have sizable cost change tied to authorization-code distribution, including provider-specific concentration at Riley's Children's Health, Fresno Heart & Surgical Hospital, and Methodist University Hospital. These records should be reconciled before tightening PA policy, changing reimbursement, or escalating provider action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Acting on a coding shift as if it were real medical trend could send UM and network teams to the wrong problem.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile PA-required coding logic and claim-level mapping in CA, IN, and TN, then restate impacted spend before any provider or policy action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The identified cost change is attributed to authorization-code distribution shifts and is flagged for validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA authorization-code distribution shifts account for +$3.6M, led by Other Kidney and Urinary Tract Diagnoses with CC at +$1.6M and Cirrhosis and Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC at +$1.5M.
IN authorization-code distribution shifts at RILEY'S CHILDREN'S HEALTH account for +$3.7M.
TN authorization-code distribution shifts at METHODIST UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL add +$576K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Behavioral health admissions and acuity are rising across NC, GA, VA, NY, IA, and WV
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Medicaid IP BH and ACUTE PSYCH
patterns_data.pattern_details: Behavioral health is a recurring cost theme across multiple states, with both inpatient behavioral health and acute psych facility growth. North Carolina and Virginia are led by depressive, stress, and adjustment-related admissions, while Georgia is concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE across both acute psych products and inpatient behavioral health. Smaller acute psych increases in New York, Iowa, and West Virginia show the same pattern of rising admissions with added unit-cost pressure.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is a scalable UM and network management opportunity because the same behavioral health pattern is repeating across products, facilities, and states.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a focused behavioral health action plan covering admission criteria, length-of-stay management, and provider concentration for IP BH and ACUTE PSYCH, starting with NC, VA, and RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE in GA.
evidence_summary: NC IP BH added +$1.5M, led by PTSD at +$684K and adjustment disorder with mixed disturbance of emotions at +$486K, with more admissions and higher paid per admit.
VA IP BH added +$1.1M, led by major depressive disorder at +$581K and depression unspecified at +$503K.
GA behavioral health totaled +$1.9M across RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE, including +$620K in TANF Standard acute psych and +$414K in TANF Foster Care acute psych.
NY, IA, and WV acute psych added another +$959K combined under ABD Non Dual or TANF Standard, with admissions and paid per admit rising.

patterns_data.pattern_details: California inpatient Med/Surg spend reflects a focused case-mix shift toward liver disease, kidney transplant complications, and a smaller set of rare high-cost admissions. The recurring liver and kidney cases suggest real acuity pressure, while bariatric surgery, transplant-related complications, and low-baseline nursing-facility cases should be validated before broad policy changes. This should be handled as a targeted clinical and validation workstream, not a general statewide inpatient rate issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Acuity shifts and rare outliers need different actions than broad utilization growth, so separating them avoids blunt network or policy responses.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send the liver disease and kidney transplant clusters for clinical pathway review, and separately validate the low-volume bariatric and NF outlier claims before policy or provider escalation.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several CA drivers are low-baseline rare cases, including small-admission outliers, so claim-level confirmation is needed before broader action.

Kidney transplant rejection added +$306K from 5 admissions with about +$31.9K paid per admit.
Rare Fresno bariatric cases added +$347K on 18 admissions.
NF added about +$215K across diabetic CKD at +$148K and obstructive or reflux uropathy at +$67K.
